# Verdicts whose wording changed with the Phase 11 rule

*Generated by `python3 -m fedverify.analysis.make_results_draft` with RESULTS_DRAFT.md; do not edit.*

Old rule: Before Phase 11: A outperforms B if the difference of their means exceeds both standard deviations over repeats; comparable if within both; otherwise not distinguishable at this sample size.

New rule: Comparisons follow one rule (Phase 11): method A outperforms method B only if the 95% patient-level bootstrap confidence interval of their paired difference excludes 0 (both run on the same folds and repeats; 2000 resamples of the patients, stratified by hospital, fixed seed); otherwise they are not distinguishable at this sample size. The mean paired difference ± its standard deviation over the repeats is reported with each interval. No p-values are given: with 5 repeats an exact test cannot go below 0.0625.

76 of 152 generated verdicts changed wording:

- 27 × "outperforms" → "is not distinguishable at this sample size from"
- 23 × "is comparable with" → "is not distinguishable at this sample size from"
- 19 × "is outperformed by" → "is not distinguishable at this sample size from"
- 4 × "is comparable with" → "outperforms"
- 1 × "is not distinguishable at this sample size from" → "is outperformed by"
- 1 × "is comparable with" → "is outperformed by"
- 1 × "is not distinguishable at this sample size from" → "outperforms"
